#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

lastPrompt: I need to you to make my mautgen template for my waybar config not move when the accent pokeball moves because rightnow there no margin on the other numbers I think.

aiTitle: Fix waybar mautgen template alignment with accent pokeball

content.text:
Found it. The "template" is your Waybar workspace module, and the culprit is exactly what you suspected.

**What's happening:** In `style.css`, only the *active* workspace button (`#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active`) has geometry — `padding: 4px`, `min-width: 20px`, and a `1px` border. The **inactive** number buttons have no matching rule, so they collapse to default size. When the pokeball moves to a new workspace, that button suddenly grows (border + padding + min-width) and shoves the other numbers over.

**The fix:** give every workspace button the same box dimensions, with a *transparent* border reserving the active button's 1px. Then only color/background changes on activation — nothing resizes.

content.text:
Fixed and reloaded live.

**What was wrong:** only the *active* workspace button had geometry — `padding: 4px`, `min-width: 20px`, and a `1px` border. Inactive number buttons had none, so they collapsed to default size. Each time the pokeball moved to a new workspace, that button suddenly gained ~10px of width (border + padding + min-width) and pushed the neighboring numbers sideways.

**What I changed in `style.css`:** added a base rule for *every* `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button` that mirrors the active box exactly — same `padding`, `margin`, `min-width/height`, `border-radius`, and a **`1px solid transparent`** border that reserves the active button's border width without drawing it. Now activating a workspace only swaps color and the pokeball background image — the box size is identical whether active or not, so the row stays put.

If anything still nudges by a pixel, it'd be worth double-checking `min-width: 20px` is wide enough for double-digit workspace numbers (10, 11…) — but that's a separate content-width question, not the pokeball shift.

content.text:
Good — the numbers themselves are now equal-width, so they no longer shift *relative to each other*. The residual movement you're seeing almost certainly isn't the numbers anymore; it's the whole **centered cluster** re-centering.

Here's why: your `modules-center` is `["hyprland/workspaces", "custom/taskbar-divider", "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar"]`, and two of those change width when you switch workspaces:

- **`custom/taskbar-divider`** — the script emits `│` only when the active workspace has open windows, and `""` when it's empty. Switching to/from an empty workspace adds/removes the glyph plus its `6px` side margins.
- **`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar`** (`active-only: true`) — shows the window icons for *only* the active workspace. Different workspaces have different window counts, so this block's width changes on every switch.

Because `modules-center` is horizontally centered, any width change there re-centers the entire group — so your workspace numbers slide a bit even though they're internally stable.

The fix depends on what you actually want, and it's your call:

questions.question: The workspace numbers slide because the centered group changes width when the taskbar icons/divider change per workspace. How do you want to stop it?

options.label: Anchor numbers left
options.description: Move hyprland/workspaces out of modules-center into modules-left so the numbers sit at a fixed position and never re-center. Taskbar stays centered.
options.preview:
modules-left:  [clock-icon, divider, clock, workspaces]
modules-center:[taskbar-divider, workspaces#taskbar]

-> numbers pinned left, never move

options.label: Reserve taskbar width
options.description: Keep layout as-is but give the taskbar + divider a fixed min-width so switching workspaces doesn't change the centered group's total width.

options.label: Always show divider
options.description: Only stop the divider from toggling (reserve its space). Helps if the divider is the main jump, but taskbar icons will still vary.
options.preview:
divider always renders (empty ws too)
-> removes divider jump only,
   window-icon width still varies

lastPrompt: The bar still moves a bit when I switch between workspaces

aiTitle: Fix waybar mautgen template alignment with accent pokeball

content.text:
No journal logs (Waybar isn't launched via systemd here), but the process list is telling, and combined with your "up/down" symptom it confirms the mechanism. Here's the diagnosis:

**The active pokeball button is the tallest thing in the bar, sitting right at the 56px height ceiling.** Its footprint = label (~22px) + `padding: 4px` (8) + `border: 1px` (2) + `margin: 4px` (8) = 40px, plus the pill's own 16px = **56px exactly**. When the `.active` class hops to a new workspace, there's a frame where that tall button isn't rendered yet, the pill briefly needs less height, Waybar recomputes, and because the bar has `margin: 4px`, the whole bar nudges up/down. (Also worth noting: your `workspace-tabs.sh` has spawned duplicate instances from reloads — harmless to this, but I'll mention it.)

**Fix:** re-add the shared-geometry rule that got reverted out (so active/inactive buttons are identical — this also keeps the horizontal fix), *and* trim the button's vertical footprint so it sits comfortably under 56px with headroom, so nothing can tip the bar over its limit.

Facts before the edits:
1. **Files referencing `style.css`:** loaded directly by Waybar; not `@import`ed anywhere (only `config.jsonc` + `style.css` in the dir).
2. **Functions/classes affected:** none (CSS). Re-adds `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button` base rule; adjusts `padding`/`margin` on the existing `.active` rule to reduce vertical height. Only workspace number buttons affected.
3. **Data files read/written:** none.
4. **User instruction verbatim:** *"No I mean like the bar moves up and down when the pokeball changes"*

content.text:
Done. Switch between a few workspaces and the bar should now hold still vertically.

**What I changed in `style.css`:**
- **Re-added the shared base rule** (`#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button`) that had been reverted out — so active and inactive buttons have identical geometry (this also preserves the horizontal no-shift fix).
- **Trimmed the vertical footprint** on both the base and `.active` rules: `padding` and `margin` went from `4px` → `2px` vertically. That drops the tallest state (the active pokeball button) from ~56px — dead against the bar's `height: 56` ceiling — down to ~48px, giving ~8px of headroom so Waybar never recomputes the bar height when the pokeball hops workspaces.

The pokeball itself will look marginally larger vertically (2px inset instead of 4px); if you'd rather keep the old inset, the alternative is bumping the bar `height` to ~60 for headroom instead — but that fights the tight 56px budget your config comments were deliberately holding.

One unrelated thing I noticed: `workspace-tabs.sh` has **duplicate instances running** (PIDs 160893 and 160910) — each Waybar reload spawns a new `socat` listener without killing the old one, so they accumulate. Harmless to this issue, but want me to add a guard so it self-cleans on reload?
